paper_title: A microwave paraphoton and axion detection experiment with 300 dB electromagnetic shielding at 3 GHz
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter chi, dimensionless (plotted as Log10 chi)
notes: Microwave light-shining-through-wall (LSW) experiment at CERN (Betz & Caspers, March 2012 run) searching for hidden photons (paraphotons) via kinetic mixing at fsys = 2.9565 GHz. No signal observed; new exclusion limit on chi presented in Fig. 2. The only explicit numerical point given in the paper text/figure annotation is m_gamma' = 1.1e-5 eV, chi = 7.6e-9, corresponding to the peak sensitivity near the cavity resonance (2.9565 GHz ~ 1.22e-5 eV). The full exclusion curve is only shown graphically (Fig. 2, log axes from ~1e-9 to 1 eV), so only the single benchmark point is extracted. LSW experiments make no dark matter density assumption. Confidence level not explicitly stated; 95% assumed as conventional.
